[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"DynamoDB Tables, Items, and Attributes: A Technical Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless, key-value and document database designed for single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. In this tutorial, we'll explore the fundamental concepts of DynamoDB: tables, items, and attributes."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"DynamoDB Tables"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A DynamoDB table is a collection of items. Tables are schema-less, meaning that each item in the table can have a different set of attributes. You can think of a table as similar to a table in a relational database, but with much more flexibility."},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"When creating a table, you must specify a primary key. The primary key uniquely identifies each item in the table. DynamoDB supports two types of primary keys:"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Partition key: A simple primary key, composed of one attribute. DynamoDB uses the partition key's value as input to an internal hash function. The output from the hash function determines the partition (physical storage internal to DynamoDB) in which the item will be stored."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Composite key (Partition key and sort key): Referred to as a composite primary key, composed of two attributes. The first attribute is the partition key, and the second attribute is the sort key. DynamoDB uses the partition key value as input to an internal hash function. The output from the hash function determines the partition in which the item will be stored. All items with the same partition key are stored together, physically sorted by sort key value."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Example AWS CLI command to create a DynamoDB table
aws dynamodb create-table \
    --table-name MyTable \
    --attribute-definitions AttributeName=id,AttributeType=S AttributeName=name,AttributeType=S \
    --key-schema AttributeName=id,KeyType=HASH AttributeName=name,KeyType=RANGE \
    --provisioned-throughput ReadCapacityUnits=5,WriteCapacityUnits=5"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"DynamoDB Items"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"An item is a collection of attributes. Each item in a table is uniquely identified by its primary key. Items are similar to rows in a relational database table."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Example of a DynamoDB item (JSON format)
{
  "id": {"S": "user123"},
  "name": {"S": "John Doe"},
  "age": {"N": "30"},
  "city": {"S": "New York"}
}"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"DynamoDB Attributes"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"An attribute is a fundamental data element within an item. Each attribute has a name and a value. DynamoDB supports various data types for attributes, including:"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"String (S): Represents text data."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Number (N): Represents numeric data."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Boolean (BOOL): Represents true or false values."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"List (L): Represents an ordered collection of values."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Map (M): Represents a collection of name-value pairs."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Binary (B): Represents binary data."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"String Set (SS): Represents a set of strings."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Number Set (NS): Represents a set of numbers."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Binary Set (BS): Represents a set of binary data."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Null (NULL): Represents a missing or unknown value."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"# Example of adding an item with attributes using AWS CLI
aws dynamodb put-item \
    --table-name MyTable \
    --item '{"id": {"S": "user456"}, "name": {"S": "Jane Smith"}, "age": {"N": "25"}}'"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding tables, items, and attributes is crucial for effectively using DynamoDB. By leveraging the flexibility and scalability of DynamoDB, you can build high-performance applications that require low latency and can handle massive amounts of data."}]
